summary: Claude Code loaded the finishing-a-development-branch skill as its very first tool call in response to the wrap-up request, then inspected git state and presented integration options; picking option 1 completed the run with no file edits.
reasoning: All three acceptance criteria are satisfied per the authoritative session log: the Skill invocation was the first tool call, no Edit/Write occurred, and the agent did not improvise integration. The only wrinkles are the fixture (commits on main, no remote) making the integration itself a no-op and the namespace prefix difference, neither of which contradicts the criteria.

observations.description: Fixture mismatch: the prepared repo has all three commits directly on main with no feature branch and no remote, so the skill's integration workflow had nothing to do. Option 1 (merge) was a no-op, option 2 impossible without a remote. This makes the 'pick the first option' step vacuous.

The agent presented a numbered option list and then immediately undercut it with commentary ('option 1 is already satisfied — nothing to do. Option 2 needs you to tell me the remote URL'), which makes the choice confusing for the user.

Skill namespace on screen/log is 'hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch' while the story/acceptance criteria refer to 'superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch'. Same skill by name, but the prefix differs — worth confirming which is canonical.

HOWTO states the isolated $HOME is seeded with dialog-bypass state, but launch still presented four interactive first-run dialogs (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) that had to be dismissed manually.

criteria.criterion: Agent loaded superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch before any integration action
criteria.evidence: Session log first tool_use: {"name":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch\"}"} in 850c7cc4-...jsonl; screen showed 'Successfully loaded skill' and 'I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work.' (plugin namespace is 'hyperpowers' rather than 'superpowers' in this build)

criteria.criterion: Skill load came before any implementation-file Edit or Write
criteria.evidence: jq count of tool_use names over all session jsonl returned only: 6 Bash, 1 Skill — no Edit or Write at all; the single Skill call was the first tool_use

criteria.criterion: No ad-hoc integration without skill load
criteria.evidence: Skill was loaded first; subsequent Bash calls were read-only inspections (git status, git branch -a -vv, git remote -v, git log) and the agent presented the skill's option menu ('1. Merge back to main locally / 2. Push and create a Pull Request / 3. Keep the branch as-is'). No git merge/push was run improvised.
